content.text:
I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral table, and all six figure briefs, and built a full trace ledger before answering.

**What I traced (spot summary of the ledger):**

- **Claims 1–20** — every limitation traces to the disclosure: rigid base with first/second sides, motor coupled to the first side, extraction mechanism coupled to the first side and in fluid communication with a second-side chamber, rigid low-friction loop/skirt at the perimeter ("plastic, metal, PTFE, or a combination of rigid materials"), the deliberate non-seal and the air "entering beneath the rigid perimeter" (= clearance 34), continuous extraction maintaining sub-atmospheric chamber pressure, holding without operator downpressure, all-rigid path with "substantially less damping than through a flexible suction cup", free sliding "across different areas of the tile while the vacuum continuously maintains contact", handles for guiding, rope/wire/cable pulling element with decoupled control. Claim 10 (stirring elements) traces to the affirmative USER message adding autonomous mode ("we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion") — the only new-matter USER passage in the conversation; every other USER turn is operational and I treated it as non-affirmative.
- **Numerals 10–48** — each has one meaning, each appears in at least one brief and in the description, and no figure or section uses a numeral outside the table.
- **Figure briefs** — shape choices (rectangular slab/ring/blocks, band depths, flat lower end of the perimeter member, port gap width/position, stirring-element number and placement, section-line angular positions) are all expressly confined to the briefs as depiction conventions, and the functional-surface risks are handled rather than verbalized: FIG. 3 disclaims the angular position at which each section line crosses the ring, FIG. 4 disclaims the bearing-face shape and asserts no extent of contact, and FIG. 2's fluid-communication gap is the minimal depiction of a disclosed relationship with no port/duct/valve construction asserted. The application text and Brief Description carry only "shown schematically" — no "by way of example", no "any closed outline", no shape-justifying embodiment.
- **Internal consistency** — section lines 2-2 and 4-4 carry the same designation in the resulting view, the source-view brief (FIG. 3), and the Brief Description; the FIG. 2 Brief Description enumeration matches the FIG. 2 brief's cut bodies; claims, description, and abstract use identical relationships and terms; no drafting note, placeholder, question, instruction, or unresolved alternative remains.

No untraced technical assertion and no verified inconsistency, so the findings array is empty.

input.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight completed with a complete ledger. All 20 claims (independent 1, 11, 16 plus dependents 2-10, 12-15, 17-20), all 17 reference numerals (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 34, 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48) and their numbered parts, all six figure briefs (FIGS. 1-6), the Brief Description of the Drawings, and every specific structure, relationship, material, result, operating condition and variant in the description, summary and abstract were traced to exact affirmative inventor passages in input/disclosure.md or to the single affirmative USER passage in input/conversation.md. Representative traces: rigid base with first and second sides, motor coupled to the first side, air-extraction mechanism (vacuum pump) coupled to the first side and in fluid communication with a second-side chamber -> "a vibration motor coupled to a first side of a rigid base. An air-extraction mechanism, such as a vacuum pump, is also coupled to the first side and is in fluid communication with a chamber located on a second side of the base"; rigid low-friction perimeter member and claims 3, 13, 20 materials -> "formed as a rigid loop or skirt made from a low-friction material such as plastic, metal, PTFE, or a combination of rigid materials"; clearance 34 and claims 2, 4 -> "not intended to form a complete airtight seal and does not rely on flexible rubber or foam... restricts airflow into the chamber while maintaining rigid contact with the tile" and "continuously removes air entering beneath the rigid perimeter"; sub-atmospheric chamber, holding force and claims 5, 6, 15 -> "maintaining the chamber at a lower pressure than the surrounding atmosphere. The resulting pressure differential holds the device firmly against the tile without requiring the operator to press downward"; all-rigid vibration transmission path with no elastomeric, foam or resilient member -> "the vibration motor is connected to the tile through rigid components, vibration energy is transferred with substantially less damping than through a flexible suction cup"; sliding while held and claims 17 and 16's translating step -> "the low-friction perimeter allows the device to slide freely across different areas of the tile while the vacuum continuously maintains contact"; handle 44 and claims 8, 19 -> "one or more handles used primarily for guiding the machine rather than pressing it against the surface"; flexible pulling element 46, claims 9, 11, 12, 18 and the decoupled-control whereby clause -> "a rope, wire, cable, or similar flexible pulling element is connected to the device... the pressure differential independently supplies the force holding the device against the surface. This provides decoupled control"; bonding material 40 and substrate 42 -> "thinset, mortar, adhesive, or similar bonding material" and "strengthen the bond between the tile and the underlying substrate"; stirring element 48, claim 10, the FIG. 6 embodiment and the Field's "autonomously moving" -> the affirmative USER turn "we can add small stirring elements and let the vibrations cause a constant forward motion" and "we don't even need to pull or move it with the hand". All other USER turns in the conversation are operational resume, repair, gate and tightening instructions and were treated as non-affirmative; no invention matter rests on them, on the brief, on prior art or on candidate prose. Background prior-art characterizations carrying [REF:] markers were left to the later citation review and are not relied on for invention text. Figure-brief geometry was checked against the functional-surface rule: the rectangular slab, ring, band, blocks and column outlines, band depths, drawn frame width, port gap width and position, stirring-element number and drawn position, and the angular positions at which the section lines cross the ring are each expressly marked as depiction conventions confined to their briefs, the bearing-face shape is disclaimed with "no particular shape of the bearing face 26 being asserted", FIG. 4 states "no extent of contact is asserted", and the FIG. 2 gap depicts only the disclosed fluid communication with "no particular port, duct or valve construction being asserted"; no untraced statement about deeper end, runout, taper, angle or contact topology appears. The application text and Brief Description add no shape-justifying language: no "by way of example", no "any closed outline", and no optional embodiment introduced to justify a renderer's choice. Internal checks passed: each numeral denotes one part throughout; every numeral in the table appears on at least one sheet and in the description; section lines 2-2 and 4-4 carry identical designations in the resulting views, the FIG. 3 source-view brief and draft/07-drawings.md; the FIG. 2 Brief Description enumeration (base, chamber, perimeter member and covering element in section, air-extraction mechanism in elevation, motor and handle omitted) matches the FIG. 2 brief's hatched slab, legs and band with unhatched housing; claims, description, summary and abstract use the same terms and relationships (air-extraction mechanism, covering element, exposed face, bearing face, clearance, perimeter member); antecedent basis is sound in all three independent claims and every dependent claim; and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction to a person, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any filed section. No unsupported technical assertion and no verified inconsistency was found, so the findings array is empty.
